newsitem.title: INDIA: India Corporation Bank IPO issue to open on Oct 3.
newsitem.headline: India Corporation Bank IPO issue to open on Oct 3.

text.p: India's public sector Corporation Bank on Tuesday said its initial public offer (IPO) of equity shares will open for subscription on October 3, 1997.
The bank is offering 38 million shares of 10 rupees face value at 80 rupees each to raise 3.04 billion rupees.
"The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has cleared Corporation Bank's draft offer document," the bank said.

"The observations made by SEBI are being incorporated in the offer document and the final version will be submitted to SEBI and the Mangalore Stock Exchange sometime during the course of this week," it said in a statement.

Of the 38 million shares, 1.9 million shares are reserved for employees and non-resident Indians, 10.2 million shares for Indian financial institutions and banks and the balance is being offered to the public, the bank said.
All subscribers except non-resident Indians need to pay only 40 rupees on application for each share and the remaining 40 rupees are to be paid on allotment.
Investors will be given the option to hold the shares in dematerialised form through National Share Depository Ltd.
The bank said its offer price of 80 rupees per share translated to a pre-issue price earning ratio of 5.24 based on profit after tax as per audited financial results for 1996/97 (April-March).
The price to book value ratio works out to 1.6 based on the book value per share of 48.72 rupees as on March 31, 1997.

"In comparison to the offer pricing of other public sector banks which had accessed the primary market in the recent past and also the current trading multiple of such banks, Corporation Bank's pricing is much more moderate despite the overall market conditions having improved considerably..," it said.
Business on the Italian exchange was slow, said traders, since foreign buyers were absent from lack of interest and the majority of domestic fund managers were on vacation.
Shares of textiles and clothing company Marzotto rose 2.8 percent to 17,490 after Kleinwort Benson issued a buy recommendation on the stock with a target price of 21,000 lire.

Seat shares rose 1.3 percent after Telecom Italia said it would acquire 20 percent of the holding company that will control the publisher, paving the way for the completion of Seat's sale to a group led by Banca Commerciale .
Banking shares were mixed, and insurers were higher.
